newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Exports to lift Amcoal year profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Exports to lift Amcoal year profit.

text.p: Export earnings boosted by the rand's depreciation may raise Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd's year profit by nearly 30 percent but gains will be slightly capped by imported inflation, analysts said on Monday.

"The depreciated rand will raise earnings and sales will be slightly up, but nothing phenomenal. Earnings per share will be up by about 30 percent," said Ross Gardiner, analyst at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Amcoal is due to announce results for the year ended March 31, 1997 on Wednesday.
Better coal prices in dollar terms in 1996 would also fuel profit, analysts said. But they added that the rand's depreciation had also started raising costs.

"There has been cost pressure over the past few months because of the knock-on effect of the rand's fall which brings in inflation. The coal business relies on machinery imported from overseas. So there is a bit of a countering effect," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
The consensus of five analysts polled by Reuters was for earnings per share of 3,408.15 cents per share compared with 2,662.1 cents previously, in a range of 3,200.00 cents to 3,500.00 cents.
They ranged the total dividend between 1,260.00 cents per share and 1,400 cents with consensus at 1,352.50 cents per share compared to 1,000 cents previously.
The group itself said last May that it was expecting a real increase in earnings for the 1996/97 financial year.
Ahead of its results, Amcoal was hardly traded on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday with only 200 shares changing hands in a single move. It was last 200 cents down at 309 rand.
